+# Desktop application
+
+[Documentation index](README.md) | [Getting started](getting-started.md) |
+[Release](release.md)
+
+2D&D can run in a secure Electron shell on macOS, Windows, and Linux while the
+GitHub Pages browser build remains unchanged. The current v1.0.0 public release
+does not include signed installers; pull requests produce short-lived unsigned
+artifacts for review.
+
+## Commands
+
+```bash
+npm run dev:desktop       # Vite renderer plus Electron shell
+npm run build:desktop     # Type-check and build dist/ + dist-electron/
+npm run test:desktop      # Production-like Electron Playwright smoke test
+npm run package:desktop   # Unsigned artifacts for the current host
+```
+
+Desktop development binds Vite to a dynamically allocated loopback port.
+Production packages load the relative Vite build from the stable
+`app://2dnd` origin.
+
+## Security boundary
+
+`electron/main.ts` owns the native process and `electron/preload.cts` exposes
+only three typed operations: read window state, toggle fullscreen, and observe
+fullscreen changes.
+
+- `contextIsolation` and Chromium sandboxing are enabled.
+- Renderer Node.js, worker Node.js, webviews, insecure content, permissions,
+  unexpected navigation, popups, and production developer tools are disabled.
+- Production renderer requests cannot reach HTTP, HTTPS, WebSocket, or other
+  remote origins.
+- External navigation is denied in-app. Only repository-owned HTTPS pages are
+  eligible to open in the operating-system browser.
+- The custom protocol resolves files only inside packaged `dist/`, with
+  traversal rejection and a restrictive Content Security Policy.
+- IPC handlers reject arguments and untrusted renderer senders.
+
+Do not expose filesystem, process, shell, command execution, arbitrary URL, or
+generic IPC APIs through preload.
+
+## Persistence
+
+The desktop shell uses the same schema-v17 `localStorage` documents as the web
+game. The stable `app://2dnd` origin keeps them available across launches and
+upgrades:
+
+| Platform | Electron user-data root |
+| --- | --- |
+| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/2D&D` |
+| Windows | `%APPDATA%\2D&D` |
+| Linux | `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/2D&D`, normally `~/.config/2D&D` |
+
+Chromium stores the documents beneath that root. Browser and desktop origins
+remain isolated; they do not silently copy or merge saves.
+
+## Packaging
+
+`electron-builder` reads the `build` configuration in `package.json`.
+`npm run generate:desktop-icons` creates repository-owned PNG, ICO, ICNS, and
+Linux icons from procedural pixel art without external assets.
+
+| Platform | Unsigned outputs |
+| --- | --- |
+| macOS | x64/arm64 DMG and ZIP |
+| Windows | x64 NSIS installer and portable executable |
+| Linux | x64 AppImage and tarball |
+
+`.github/workflows/desktop.yml` builds and smoke-tests each platform before
+uploading versioned review artifacts. Public distribution still requires human
+code-signing credentials: Apple Developer ID plus notarization for macOS and an
+appropriate Authenticode certificate for Windows. Credentials must stay in the
+release environment, never in source or pull-request workflows.

## Issue: Windows installer is overwritten by portable build
**File:** /Users/mbianchidev/.copilot/copilot-worktrees/2dnd/cp-desktop-vigilant-waddle/package.json:59  
**Severity:** High  
**Problem:** NSIS and portable targets resolve to the same `.exe` artifact name, so only the portable executable remains.  
**Evidence:** Windows packaging logged both targets writing `release/2D-and-D-1.0.0-win-x64.exe`; the release directory contains one executable plus an orphaned NSIS blockmap.  
**Suggested fix:** Configure distinct target-specific names, such as `-setup.exe` and `-portable.exe`.

## Issue: Desktop development command cannot launch on Windows
**File:** /Users/mbianchidev/.copilot/copilot-worktrees/2dnd/cp-desktop-vigilant-waddle/hacks/run-desktop-dev.mjs:63  
**Severity:** Medium  
**Problem:** Windows selects `vite.cmd` and `electron.cmd`, then passes them directly to `spawn()` without a shell. Node cannot directly execute `.cmd` wrappers on Windows.  
**Evidence:** Both spawn calls use the generated `.cmd` paths with the default `shell: false`.  
**Suggested fix:** Invoke JavaScript entry points with `process.execPath`, or explicitly use `cmd.exe`/`shell: true` on Windows.

## Issue: Changed development-host policy leaves required CI failing
**File:** /Users/mbianchidev/.copilot/copilot-worktrees/2dnd/cp-desktop-vigilant-waddle/src/config.ts:17  
**Severity:** Medium  
**Problem:** The new loopback-only behavior contradicts the existing `isLocalDev` test, causing every PR build to fail.  
**Evidence:** `npm test` failed at `tests/config.test.ts:31` with 956 tests passing and one failure. The PR workflow runs this suite at `.github/workflows/pr.yml:28`.  
**Suggested fix:** Update the stale test to expect `false` for `github.io.example.com` if the loopback-only policy is intentional.
The pre-CI review found three concrete blockers: Windows artifact name collision, Windows `.cmd` spawning, and a stale local-dev test. I’m fixing all three before the full gate.

input.title: Package 2D&D as a secure Electron desktop app
input.body:
## Summary

- add a sandboxed Electron 43 shell with a stable `app://2dnd` origin, restrictive CSP/network/navigation policy, typed fullscreen preload bridge, and crash diagnostics
- add procedural desktop icons, cross-platform electron-builder targets, and macOS/Windows/Linux unsigned artifact CI
- add production-like Electron Playwright coverage for fullscreen, real character creation, schema-v17 save persistence, relaunch, and continue
- document desktop development, storage isolation, security boundaries, packaging, signing, testing, and release operations

## Validation

- `npm ci`
- `npm audit`
- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm test` (962 tests)
- `npm run test:browser` (26 tests)
- `npm run test:desktop` (1 production-like Electron flow)
- `npm run build`
- `npm run build:desktop`
- `npm run package:desktop` (macOS x64/arm64 DMG + ZIP)
- `git diff --check`

Closes #162
